'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[US–UK airstrikes on Yemen]]
***A [[Greece|Greek]]-owned [[bulk carrier]] is hit by a [[missile]] launched from [[Houthi movement|Houthi]]-controlled territory in [[Yemen]] with minor damage reported. Separately, the [[United States]] launches more [[airstrike]]s on Houthi positions, destroying four [[anti-ship missile]]s that were being prepared for launch. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-67992600 (BBC News)]
***British [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[petroleum|oil]] and [[natural gas|gas]] company [[Shell plc|Shell]] suspends all [[Red Sea]] shipments indefinitely amid Houthi attacks on commercial vessels. [https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/shell-suspends-all-red-sea-shipments-indefinitely-houthi-attacks-yemen-report (Fox Business)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)| Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Bombing of Kharkiv]]
***Seventeen people are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[missile strike]] on a residential area in [[Kharkiv]], Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-missiles-hit-ukraines-kharkiv-wounding-4-officials-say-2024-01-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Iran–Pakistan border skirmishes]]
**[[2024 Iranian missile strikes in Pakistan]]
***[[Iran]] launches [[ballistic missile]]s at [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], targeting what it claims are [[Jaish ul-Adl]] terrorist sites, killing two children and injuring three other people. Pakistan calls the action an "unprovoked violation" of its airspace. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-iraq-militant-bases-attack-05c7530d66fb05dd6f2868527003ba2d (AP)]
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict (2022–present)|Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions]] 
**A [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] soldier is killed and two others are arrested by the [[Rwandan Army]] in a cross-border incident in [[Rubavu District]], [[Rwanda]]. [https://apnews.com/article/rwanda-congo-military-border-c53d5f990fe285e784b30c2c6d8c841e (AP)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**An [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] [[suicide attack|suicide bomber]] kills three people and wounds two others outside of the [[Mayor of Mogadishu]]'s office in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/suicide-attack-rocks-somali-capital-mogadishu/3110171 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sudan]] suspends its membership in the [[Intergovernmental Authority on Development]] (IGAD) after accusing it of inviting [[Rapid Support Forces]] official [[Hemedti]] to an upcoming summit in [[Kampala]], [[Uganda]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-burhan-dagalo-war-africa-e8fd4600ea0dc83e916958a3edfcd4bb (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases]]
**A lawsuit is filed against [[Madison Square Garden Entertainment]] chairman [[James Dolan (businessman)|James Dolan]], accusing him of pressuring a woman into having unwanted sex in 2014. The woman also files a lawsuit against film producer [[Harvey Weinstein]], accusing him of sexually assaulting her. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/01/16/arts/music/james-dolan-harvey-weinstein-sexual-assault-lawsuit.html (''The New York Times'')]
*A [[drive-by shooting]] kills five people in [[Ceiba, Puerto Rico]]. Authorities say the killings are likely connected to [[Illegal drug trade|drug trafficking]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/police-people-including-teenage-boy-killed-drive-shooting-106407016 (ABC News)]
*The [[Government of Iran|Iranian government]] extends [[Nobel laureate]] [[Narges Mohammadi]]'s jail term of 12 years for "spreading propaganda". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-67986227.amp (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Rwanda asylum plan]]
**[[United Kingdom|UK]] [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] deputy chairmen [[Lee Anderson]] and [[Brendan Clarke-Smith]] resign to join 60 other Conservative [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MPs]] in voting to back an amendment to the [[Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Bill|Asylum and Immigration Bill]], making it more strict. The amendment later fails to pass. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-67999810 (BBC News)]
